items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I did Liza Minelli's "Cabaret" over there

ctx.x: So then you have to talk to him in musical terms and say, well, if you use double stops, you can use 12, and if you get the right musicians. So I can talk to them from that standpoint, musically, and I really don't have any problems with them. We've cut the budget considerably since I've been here.

Now over at ABC, the type of things that I always did -- I did all the soundtrack albums. I did Liza Minelli's "Cabaret" over there; I did "The Song of Norway", "Lovers and Other Strangers" -- and as I said before I went to New York, and I did the Broadway show, which we were up for a Grammy for it -- I think we came in 2nd, and nobody ever remembers 2nd -- but I'll tell you.

But I really came over here to do a jazz label. That was why I left ABC, because my deal here was we're gonna start a jazz label and I was going to do it. That's what I am supposed to start in January.
